Really grateful to Carnegie Mellon University Mellon College of Science for the feature and the opportunity to share about the work I've been doing! I'm especially thankful to Rajdeep Sarma and Yiwen Wang who first brought me into research and have given me so many opportunities to meaningfully learn, grow, and contribute through their mentorship.

A month ago I was playing in the NBA Finals. This weekend I was on the other side of the whiteboard, coaching the Jr. EYBL nationals. Harper U , the program my brother Ron, my mom and I built in New Jersey, made it to nationals in North Augusta. My mom coached me from first grade all the way through high school. This weekend she was right there coaching alongside me, and having her on my side of the huddle for once felt like everything had come full circle. Coming back to this scene straight from a season in the NBA, I saw it differently than I ever did as a kid. I wasn't just there to watch. I spent the weekend making calls on what Harper U does differently from here. Our guys left everything they had on the floor, and I don't know if I've ever been prouder of a group of guys. What's one thing you'd want to see us add to Harper U?

I am excited to share that this past May, I graduated from Quinnipiac University . During my time at Quinnipiac, I had the opportunity to pursue majors in Economics, Mathematics, and Data Science while working alongside faculty and fellow students who challenged me to think rigorously and pursue research I genuinely enjoyed. These experiences sparked my interest in quantitative macroeconomics, econometrics, and dynamic economic modeling. I am incredibly grateful to Donn Johnson , Christopher Ball , Jesse Kalinowski, Aman Desai , Jill Shahverdian , and all of the mentors, friends, and family who supported me throughout my undergraduate journey. I am also excited to share that this fall I will be joining the University of Rochester as a Ph.D. student in Economics, continuing to develop my research interests while contributing to the department's research community. Thank you to everyone who has been part of this journey, and I look forward to what lies ahead.

From the legendary 1970 Championship squad that paved the way to the 1973 NBA Champions and our unstoppable 2026 Champions—the wait is finally over! The crown has been passed to Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns from Walt Frazier and Willis Reed. Two legendary eras, one proud city. The New York Knicks are the 2026 NBA Champions and I feel the pride and joy of my 13 year old self once again. From left to right, pictured in the 2026 photo is OG Anunoby (#8), Jalen Brunson (#11 and raising a cup), Karl-Anthony Towns (#32), Josh Hart (#3), and Mikal Bridges. From left to right, pictured in the 1970 photo is Dick Barnett (shirtless), Walt "Clyde" Frazier (raising a cup in the polo-style shirt), Bill Bradley (shirtless, laughing with mouth open), Dave DeBusschere (#22), and Willis Reed (in the white polo with NY logo). In 1986, I stood among millions of ecstatic fans in the Canyon of Heroes, completely buried in confetti as lower Broadway celebrated the New York Mets' historic World Series victory. Watching Dwight Gooden, Keith Hernandez, Lenny Dykstra, Wally Backman, Mookie Wilson, Gary Carter, Ron Darling, and Darryl Strawberry wave from classic convertible cars is a memory I will never forget. It was a legendary New York moment, and if you ever get the chance to witness a ticker-tape parade in person, you absolutely cannot miss it. The Knicks championship ticker-tape parade will take place on Thursday, June 18 at 10AM near Battery Park and will travel north along Broadway in Lower Manhattan. It will conclude at City Hall, where Mayor Zohran Mamdani will host a ceremony to present the team with the Key to the City. This historic victory officially restores the Championship back to New York, proving that our 53-year wait was well worth every single moment.

Excited to share ALOE, an open-source repository for fast molecular screening that I designed and built as part of the EQUUS project at Cavall Labs and the Garcia-Bosch Lab at CMU. I led the software side of the project, working closely with chemistry collaborators to shape the use cases and build a modular, scalable foundation for efficient molecular screening workflows. It’s been rewarding to contribute to interdisciplinary work that brings together chemistry, computation, and mathematics, and I can't wait to see how the community builds on it.

I am incredibly excited and proud to announce that I have recieved my Private Pilots License! As an aeronautical engineer, this first step into the other side of aviation has not only broadened my knowledge of aerospace, but has also given me a lot of insight to what safety really means when you are behind the controls of an aircraft. I would like to thank my CFI Shane Grubbs and the rest of the team at Fly Corps Aviation for their instruction and patience; I couldn’t have done it without them. I would also like to thank my manager Todd Barber for allowing me to pursue this license as a part of the Gulfstream Aerospace Flight Training Reimbursement Program. Finally I would like to shoutout Darren Pan and Alex Zhuo for the flights they have taken me on that inspired me to pursue my own liscense. Cheers to blue skies. 🛩️

This past month, I’m incredibly grateful to graduate from Purdue University with B.S. degrees in Computer Science and Mathematics. Purdue has challenged me, shaped me, and given me opportunities I never could have imagined — from research and internships to leadership experiences and lifelong friendships. The culmination of these experiences and the support of the communities around me led to the incredible honor of serving as the Banner Bearer for the College of Science at commencement. I’m especially thankful to the professors, mentors, friends, teammates, and family members who supported me throughout this journey. As one chapter closes, I’m excited to begin the next one this summer as a Software Engineer at Google , joining the IOS App Ads team under Wenxing Ye . I’m incredibly grateful to learn from and work alongside such talented people, and looking forward to my new experiences as a Noogler! Boiler Up forever! 🚂

Figured I should follow up my graduation post with what I am doing next. I am excited to share that this fall I will be joining the University of Oxford to pursue a PhD (or DPhil) in Engineering Science. I look forward to joining the Oxford community, learning from world-class researchers, and contributing to impactful research in the years ahead. Thank you to everyone who has been part of this journey so far. I'm excited to see what comes next!
